description: A fist-sized wad of translucent grey-blue matter, dragging itself along on limbs it improvises and discards.  Core sample 7: motile at minus forty.  Not a bacterium, not a fungus, not anything with a name.
A heaving slab of the permafrost organism, big as a sled dog, its surface crazed with frost patterns that move against the light.  When we warm it, it grows.  When we cool it, it waits.

A room-swallowing tide of grey-blue matter that has long since stopped resembling a sample of anything.  Four hundred metres of permafrost held this for a hundred thousand years.  The freezer door held it for six weeks.

The heart of the organism: a dense, faintly luminous core around which the lesser masses arrange themselves like petals.  It does not move much.  It does not need to.  Reykjavik said keep feeding it and log everything.

A squat, short-legged reindeer with a coat like a snowdrift, pawing through the crust for buried moss.  The smallest and northernmost reindeer in the world, and one of the only warm things left on this island.

An adult polar bear, yellow-white against the snow and utterly unafraid of you.  On this archipelago it was illegal to leave the settlement without a rifle, and the bears were the entire reason.  The settlements have stopped enforcing much of anything.
